title: Eyes on Samsung Q2 Earnings, IMF's Korea Growth Revision
snippet: Samsung Electronics reports Q2 preliminary earnings this week, with the market expecting around 90 trillion won, while the IMF is set to sharply revise
extractedText: Eyes on Samsung Q2 Earnings, IMF's Korea Growth RevisionFX Market Opens for 24-Hour Trading from MondayFinance|Published 2026.07.05. 06:00:05|By Han Dong-hoon|Summary|SaveAAASamsung Electronics' Seocho office building in Seoul. Yonhap NewsSamsung Electronics' (005930.KS) preliminary second-quarter earnings are the top focus this week. The International Monetary Fund (IMF) will release its revised growth forecast for Korea.Samsung Electronics will announce its preliminary second-quarter earnings Monday. Micron Technology, considered a bellwether for the semiconductor industry, earlier posted record earnings, raising expectations that Samsung Electronics will also deliver record-breaking results. First-quarter operating profit reached an all-time high of 57 trillion won, and the market expects around 90 trillion won for the second quarter.The IMF will release its "July World Economic Outlook" on Tuesday. The IMF issues economic forecasts for the world and member countries four times a year, in January, April, July, and October. In April, it presented Korea's real gross domestic product (GDP) growth forecast for this year at 1.9 percent, unchanged from January. Since the IMF's announcement, Korea's first-quarter growth has surged and semiconductor exports have hit record monthly highs, prompting expectations of a significant upward revision this time. The Bank of Korea (BOK) and the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) have already raised their forecasts to 2.6 percent, while some foreign research institutions have offered figures as high as 4 percent.The Bank of Korea will release its "May Balance of Payments" the same day. On the back of strong semiconductor exports, the cumulative surplus through the end of April this year exceeded 100 billion dollars. That is more than four times the figure for the same period last year and already surpasses the entire surplus recorded in 2024. With strong exports continuing across non-semiconductor items as well as semiconductors, the large surplus trend is expected to have persisted.The Seoul foreign exchange market, Korea's domestic FX market, will open around the clock starting Monday. Previously, won-dollar trading hours ran from 9 a.m. to 2 a.m. the following day, but they will now change to from 6 a.m. Monday to 6 a.m. Saturday. Trading will continue on public holidays, with only weekends and January 1 excluded. While currency exchange will become more convenient and market access will improve, some forecast that short-term volatility could intensify further.Overseas, attention should be paid to the minutes of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting in June. Last month's meeting was the first FOMC held under Chairman Kevin Warsh, and while the statement and dot plot were assessed as hawkish, the press conference offered no clear signal on the future policy direction.
